      "observations": [
        "All four owned diffs and the complete new test were read. CalDAV state becomes a plural address array and the offline cached-property name changes with it. Discovery keeps only mailto entries, lowercases them and removes duplicates with Set while retaining encounter order; no preferred-address sort is implemented.",
        "Discovery assigns a new list only when filtered mailto entries exist. The empty-result branch does not explicitly clear an earlier list. The tests do not cover repeated discovery, empty-response clearing or cached-property migration.",
        "isInvitation first requires an organizer ID, caches the first attendee for each lowercase ID in one Map, rejects a matching organizer alias, then accepts a matching attendee alias. If alias checks do not decide, the non-ACL explicit/organizer property fallback and ACL owner-identity fallback remain.",
        "getInvitedAttendee returns a resolved organizerId attendee first, then the first matching ACL owner identity, then the first matching calendar alias, and finally null. These ordered fallbacks and the distinction between Map.has and Map.get preserve object-return versus Boolean roles.",
        "Multiple-address matching does not apply uniformly to transport consumers. organizerId, free/busy organizer, sender fallback, explicit REPLY attendee lookup and outbox sender still use the first address in their stated branches. Existing lesson b7aeebe652aa261ba7a390d2a1c326a409c52446c9d9f0a63cc1deea13e8eddc covers collection/first-address fallback; no server preference guarantee is inferred.",
        "The organizer fallback changes statically: the prior ACL branch tried the parent for a missing organizer object or ID. The new organizer || parent expression tries the parent only for a missing/falsy object, then rejects a selected object without an ID. CalAttendee permits a null ID and CalItemBase stores the organizer object without an ID check. No incoming-event instance or affected runtime path was reproduced, and the added test does not cover this distinction.",
        "The owned fillACLProperties first-address branch and existing ACL override are retained separately from the later accepted configured-identity priority and mailto-prefixed ACL identity. Current behavior must not be attributed wholly to this original patch.",
        "The iTIP helper handles a resolvable X-MOZ-INVITED-ATTENDEE before delegating to scheduling support and falls through if the property does not resolve. Existing lesson 1d49bb04b196b0af81cd5d6cc3a7f509baee948f228eb6f5d84634ed7afe5969 covers that distinct entry-point contract.",
        "The seven changed assertions set calendarUserAddresses on a memory calendar. They directly check a middle alias for invitation/attendee lookup, no match, an empty list and organizer membership. Every message is nonempty. They do not test network discovery, ACL owners, mixed-case inputs, preferred ordering, duplicate IDs, explicit CalDAV sending or the parent-organizer edge.",
        "The complete primary Bug includes the initial alias failure, a rendered early three-file patch proposal, the author's explicit not-review-ready/GPT-assisted/manual-test account, the final patch locator/landing and later backport instructions. The early calItipUtils proposal is not part of the final four-file owned diff. Backport/Pastebin instructions remain historical text, not a recommendation or executed action.",
        "D273346's full creation-to-final timeline, all 40 actual inline bodies (including two exact old-diff threads) and both actual summary pairs were read. The summary edits change review tags, not implementation. The alias matching tests and one cached attendee map were adopted; the proposed preferred-address sorting and filter/map constructor alternative were not.",
        "The reviewer initially asks to remove null/optional guards, the author explains that local calendars lack the property, and the reviewer acknowledges the correction. Separately, the requested organizerId || null fallback is explicitly withdrawn after the reviewer notices the length guard. Neither rejected suggestion is treated as an adopted contract.",
        "The reviewer asks to retain the old non-ACL fallback and the author agrees after the new alias checks. Ordering, Map.has/includes, explicit null return and first-match loop suggestions were compared with landed source. Historical Fastmail/SoGo reports and an acceptance conditional on a test run do not prove current server behavior or fresh execution."
